summary: GPU allocator aging causing midday throughput tailspin for dedicated tenant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a sharp drop in dedicated pool throughput starting ~2026-03-10 11:30 UTC impacting PrismHealth's production routes. Symptoms include elevated p95/p99 latency, increased queueing, and requests falling back to lower-tier models. The degradation recovers only after operator intervention (restarting allocator processes).

Impact:
- PrismHealth observed 3x increase in p99 for text-generation routes and ~40% drop in throughput for pinned model redwood-small-ops-3b.
- Multiple retries and client-side fallback to hosted models triggered higher token costs.
- User-facing slowdowns during midday window for the US-East reserved pool.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (reserved pool id: rp-89c2)
description_continued:
- Region: us-east, prod
- Customer tier: dedicated
- Affected services: serving-runtime, allocator, autoscaler, scheduler

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Heavy mix of long-lived streaming and many short-lived inference requests during midday traffic spike.
2. Allocator shows steadily increasing average slot age and queue depth.
3. New short streams are queued behind aged allocations; autoscaler does not scale fast enough because allocator believes pool is saturated.
4. Throughput drops and p99 latency increases; requests begin failing over to fallback routing after configured timeouts.

Relevant logs / traces (excerpts):
- allocator WARN 2026-03-10T11:38:21Z "slot_age_skew > threshold (mean=98s, p95=420s)"
- scheduler DEBUG 2026-03-10T11:39:05Z "assign_attempts=3; queued_short_streams=172; active_long_streams=43"
- autoscaler INFO 2026-03-10T11:40:12Z "scale_decision=hold; signal=low_free_slots; reason=allocator_reports_high_util"
- serving-runtime ERROR 2026-03-10T11:41:00Z "prefetch_latency=1.8s; kv-cache-growth=+18% in 10m"

Notes: allocator aging refers to the distribution of allocation ages (how long a GPU slot has been occupied). We observed a skewed distribution where many slots are long-lived and not releasing quickly (old streaming sessions + pinned prefetched contexts), while short-lived bursts pile up and are starved. This is different from classic noisy-tenant GPU hogging — allocator metrics suggested internal bookkeeping that caused late-stage allocation reordering and a conservative free-slot estimate to be published to the autoscaler.
comments: 2026-03-10 12:02 - Support (Alex Morales): Opened with priority P1 after first customer alert. Collected initial traces, escalated to SRE and Allocator team.

2026-03-10 12:25 - SRE (Priya Singh): Correlated tenant's traffic with allocator age histogram. Noted allocator reported mean slot age high and an unexpected high variance. Kicked off a controlled restart of allocator service for rp-89c2; initial recovery observed (~30% throughput).

2026-03-10 13:10 - Allocator Eng (Brian Lee): Found allocator GC path did not evict ephemeral slot descriptors when a streaming session extended beyond estimate. Working on patch to refresh age counters and improve eviction heuristics. Linked PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/229
2026-03-11 09:42 - Customer (PrismHealth SRE): Reporting improved but still see intermittent p99 spikes around 11:00-13:00 UTC. Requested confirmation of root-cause and durable fix timeline.

2026-03-12 08:05 - Priya Singh: We reproduced locally with a mix of long streams + many short streams, confirmed allocator-age skew triggers conservative autoscaler hold. Patch under review; scheduling hotfix rollout tonight with offline warmup to avoid flapping.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Noisy neighbor long streams hold GPU slots for longer than allocator expected; combined with a bug in age accumulation, leading to inflated utilization estimates.
Hypothesis B: Autoscaler input pipeline consumed allocator's free-slot metric which was stale due to a concurrency bug; autoscaler chose not to scale even though real free capacity existed.
Telemetry: Age histogram, slot churn rate, and prefetch/kv-cache growth tracked show correlation with p99 latency spikes. NVLink stats normal. Driver-level OOMs not observed.
Repro: Synthetic workload (50 long streams + bursty 200 short requests/min) reproduces slowdown within 8-12 minutes in staging using the same allocator codepath.
Mitigation trial: Restarting allocator processes cleared the stale free-slot estimate and restored normal scaling behavior; indicates allocator internal state drift as root cause.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied: rolled allocator hotfix v1.3.7 to rp-89c2 (patch refreshes age counters and fixes concurrency path for free-slot reporting). In addition: added temporary conservative autoscaler override to allow scaling on observed queue depth while patch rollout verifies. Outcome: throughput restored to baseline for PrismHealth routes; p99 reduced to previous levels during monitored windows. Follow-ups: 1) full rollout across reserved pools scheduled 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC with blue/green to avoid broad impact; 2) add an allocator health signal (slot_age_skew) to PagerDuty threshold; 3) update runbook to include controlled allocator restart steps and to check kv-cache growth as early indicator. Customer notified of remediation plan and timeline.
final_status_notes: Hotfix verified in prod for rp-89c2. Monitoring for 72h. High-priority follow-up tasks tracked in INT-1372 (allocator observability) and PR-229 for code fix. Customer acknowledged initial remediation and asked for postmortem; postmortem scheduled.
